## P99 — EXPANDED SECURITY CONTENT


Scenario: payment authorization architecture. Auth flow: OAuth2 Authorization Code + PKCE with Python backend. Token structure: access_token (JWT, RS256, 15min TTL) + refresh_token (opaque, 30 day TTL, rotation on use). Token storage: httpOnly secure SameSite=Strict cookie for web, secure storage for mobile. Protection: CSRF token for state-changing requests, CORS allowlist with specific origins only, rate limiting per user (100 req/min). Session invalidation: on password change, on logout, on suspicious activity detection. Audit: log every auth event with user_id, IP, user_agent, timestamp.

Scenario: inventory output-encoding penetration test findings. Finding: RCE in inventory API endpoint. CVSS score: 8.5 (HIGH). Attack path: unvalidated input parameter allows RCE via crafted payload. Exploit: curl -X POST https://api.example.com/inventory/search -d "query=malicious_payload" — returns 200 with data from other tenants. Fix: input validation with allowlist regex, parameterized queries, tenant isolation check in middleware. Retest: pass after fix — payload returns 400 with validation error. Regression test: added to security test suite.

Scenario: user-profile secrets-mgmt compliance review. Regulation: SOC2 + GDPR + PCI-DSS for user-profile module. Data classification: customer PII (GDPR), payment data (PCI-DSS), authentication data (SOC2). Controls: encryption at rest (AES-256-GCM), encryption in transit (TLS 1.3), access logging with immutable audit trail, data retention policy (delete PII after 90 days of account closure), breach notification within 72 hours, annual penetration test, quarterly access review. Evidence: automated compliance report generated weekly, stored for auditor access. Gap: encryption key rotation not automated — manual process with 90-day rotation.

Verification: SAST (Semgrep rule for mass assignment), DAST (OWASP ZAP), manual code review of all database access paths, unit test for injection resistance. Regression: add to security test suite, CI gate on SAST findings.

Architecture: auth authentication on Rust. Auth: OAuth2 Authorization Code + PKCE, access_token JWT RS256 15min TTL, refresh_token opaque 30d TTL with rotation. Storage: httpOnly secure SameSite=Strict cookie for web, Keychain for mobile. CSRF: double-submit cookie pattern. CORS: allowlist origins only. Rate limit: 100 req/min per user. Session: invalidate on password change, logout, suspicious activity. Audit: log every auth event with user_id, IP, user_agent, timestamp.

Session: invalidate on password change, logout, suspicious activity. Audit: log every auth event with user_id, IP, user_agent, timestamp.

Session: invalidate on password change, logout, suspicious activity. Audit: log every auth event with user_id, IP, user_agent, timestamp.

Threat model: STRIDE-M for payment output-encoding. Asset: customer PII (email, phone, address, payment fingerprints). Spoofing: attacker impersonates user via stolen session token. Tampering: transaction amount modified in transit. Repudiation: user claims unauthorized transaction without audit trail. Info disclosure: DB backup exposed. DoS: auth endpoint flooded. EoP: regular user escalates to admin. Controls: each threat mapped to specific control with test verification. Residual risk: LOW after all controls verified.

EoP: regular user escalates to admin. Controls: each threat mapped to specific control with test verification. Residual risk: LOW after all controls verified.

Dependencies: payment C# — 150 direct deps. Scan: C# audit + Trivy. Findings: 12 vulns (3 critical, 5 high, 4 moderate). Critical CVE: serialization library RCE — update to 2.1.3. High CVE: HTTP library request smuggling — update to 4.0.0. Moderate: old TLS library weak ciphers — update to 1.3.0. Process: CI scan, fail build on critical/high, auto-PR for non-breaking updates, monthly full audit with SCA tool. SBOM: generated with CycloneDX format, published to artifact registry.

Cloud: auth on AWS with Rust. IAM: least privilege roles per service, no human users in production. Network: VPC with private subnets for services, public only for load balancers. WAF: OWASP CRS rules, rate limiting, IP allowlist for admin endpoints. Security groups: per-service ingress/egress rules, deny all by default. Encryption: S3/KMS with customer-managed keys, EBS encrypted by default. Monitoring: GuardDuty/Security Command Center, CIS benchmark compliance scanning, config rules for non-compliant resources.

Incident: payment security breach. Scenario: attacker exploited path traversal in payment API. Discovery: CrowdStrike alert on anomalous outbound traffic. Containment: block malicious IPs at WAF, rotate all secrets, isolate affected service. Eradication: patched vulnerability, verified clean backup, rebuilt instances from known-good image. Recovery: restore from pre-incident backup, verify data integrity, gradual traffic restoration. Lessons: [P0] add path traversal detection to SAST, [P1] improve network segmentation, [P2] tabletop exercise for similar scenarios.


Incident: inventory security breach. Scenario: attacker exploited IDOR in inventory API. Discovery: CrowdStrike alert on anomalous outbound traffic. Containment: block malicious IPs at WAF, rotate all secrets, isolate affected service. Eradication: patched vulnerability, verified clean backup, rebuilt instances from known-good image. Recovery: restore from pre-incident backup, verify data integrity, gradual traffic restoration. Lessons: [P0] add IDOR detection to SAST, [P1] improve network segmentation, [P2] tabletop exercise for similar scenarios.

Container: auth Rust container security. Base: distroless non-root image (UID 10001). Build: multi-stage (builder + runtime), scan with Trivy in CI, fail on critical/high CVEs. Registry: private registry with image signing (cosign), vulnerability scanning on push, tag immutability for production. Orchestration: pod security standards (restricted), network policies (default deny), OPA/Gatekeeper policies for compliance.

Registry: private registry with image signing (cosign), vulnerability scanning on push, tag immutability for production. Orchestration: pod security standards (restricted), network policies (default deny), OPA/Gatekeeper policies for compliance.

Crypto: payment Rust encryption design. At rest: AES-256-GCM with key per data type. Key management: KMS with automatic rotation (1 year). Transit: TLS 1.3 with HSTS, mTLS for service-to-service. Application: encryption per-field for PII using envelope encryption. Hashing: bcrypt for passwords (cost 12), SHA-256 for integrity checks, HMAC for request signing. Key rotation: process documented, automated with 30-day key rotation for application keys, 90-day for encryption keys. Audit: every encryption/decryption operation logged.

IDS/IPS: network-based detection with Suricata, alert on known attack patterns. DDoS: CloudFront/Cloudflare shielding, AWS Shield Advanced. Monitoring: VPC Flow Logs analyzed with Athena, alert on unusual traffic patterns.

Audit: auth audit logging. Events: all access to PII, all auth events (login, logout, failure), all configuration changes, all privilege escalations, all data export operations. Format: structured JSON with actor_id, action, resource, timestamp, source_ip, geo_location, outcome. Storage: append-only log stream (AWS CloudTrail / GCP Audit Logs), immutable S3 bucket with object lock, 7-year retention. Monitoring: real-time alert on audit log tampering, anomaly detection on audit event patterns. Review: weekly automated analysis, quarterly manual review.

Storage: append-only log stream (AWS CloudTrail / GCP Audit Logs), immutable S3 bucket with object lock, 7-year retention. Monitoring: real-time alert on audit log tampering, anomaly detection on audit event patterns. Review: weekly automated analysis, quarterly manual review.

Storage: append-only log stream (AWS CloudTrail / GCP Audit Logs), immutable S3 bucket with object lock, 7-year retention. Monitoring: real-time alert on audit log tampering, anomaly detection on audit event patterns. Review: weekly automated analysis, quarterly manual review.

---
*Synarc S2 risk hard floors, S13 quality gates, S17 zero-tolerance violations apply. Ledger entry for every threat model, security review, and vulnerability.*

*Security risk floors CANNOT be lowered. Auth/payment/PII/secrets/access control changes are CRITICAL minimum. All security changes are at least HIGH.*

*This plugin is the single comprehensive security plugin. It absorbs and supersedes security-patterns and compliance-analyst. All security reasoning lives here.*
